howto_md:
## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of technology in two trunks: **things** (devices, appliances, machines and tools) and **fields** (technology applied to textiles, medicine, space, money and more). Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what it is, the idea behind it, who began it and where it stands now. Every entry has an ID (such as TEC-03.1 for the refrigerator) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches.
- **Sections (TEC-01, TEC-02...)** are the main topics; many open with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have used, opened or understood it.
- **Registers** give 30 landmark technologies with their Indian contribution, a timeline from stone tools to AI and the major awards (checked 13 November 2026).
- **Tags** (#smartphone #energy #ai) and **See also** links connect related pages.
- Start with **Part 0**, seven two-minute questions from stone tools to today's frontier.
howto_intro: This booklet is a map of technology: electronic devices, home appliances, mechanical devices and machines, tools, and technology in every field from textiles to AI. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters.
Every entry has an ID (such as TEC-03.1 for the refrigerator). The same ID is the entry's address on curioussparoows.com, where each one is growing into its own page.
howto_boxes: **Parts:** the intro questions, the master map, devices and appliances, machines and tools, fields (two Parts), registers, people and institutions, ideas, the practical guide, reviews, navigation and sources.
**Sub-sections and entries (☐):** one or two lines each.
**Registers:** 30 landmark technologies, the timeline and awards. They are a sourced selection; the full lists grow on the website.
**Step 2.** Walk through your own home with Part 2.
**Step 3.** Pick a field you care about in Parts 4 and 5.
**Step 4.** Follow tags to music, films, cooking and crafts.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you learn, and keep a maker's log.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 12, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
